Theorem
[Dirichlet Uniqueness] 1. ch10:10.2\group chapter-10 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0276 ↗ gilbarg-trudinger.thm.10.1.comparison-principle Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1, if $Qu=Qv$ in $\Omega $ and $u=v$ on $\partial \Omega $, then $u=v$ in $\Omega $.
Proof

\sketch Apply the comparison principle in both directions.

□

Theorems 10.1 and 10.2 also hold for $u,v\in C^0(\overline\Omega )\cap C^1(\Omega ) \cap W^{2,n}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega )$ by the strong-solution maximum principle.
